question.text: For a Automotive use case involving automotive radar, where would Vector Network Analyzer fit in the test workflow?

messages.text: For a Automotive use case involving automotive radar, where would Vector Network Analyzer fit in the test workflow?

A Vector Network Analyzer would fit **upstream of the automotive radar echo-generation / scenario test**, in the **electrical-interface, PCB/PCBA, cable/connector, and transmission-channel validation** part of the workflow, while the automotive radar functional scenario test itself is covered by an automotive radar echo generator such as the R&S AREG800A, which performs dynamic artificial object generation for radar under test, including FMCW radar distance generation up to 3000 m [4].
In that upstream validation workflow, network analyzers are listed among instruments used for transmission-channel and DUT/test-board validation challenges, including the transmission channel, measurement path to the DUT, test-board development, power distribution network, ADC/DAC frontend performance, reference-clock/PLL jitter performance, and interface testing [6]. In the PCB / high-speed digital test workflow, the relevant measurement stages are material measurement, material/stackup selection, signal-integrity modeling/testing, sampling testing, and process monitoring [10][22]. The measurements called out there include impedance / TDR, Dk/Df extraction, insertion loss, roughness, crosstalk, transmission-line modeling, eye diagram, Delta-L, ISD/ADK, and cable/connector testing [10].
A concrete VNA example in the passages is the R&S ZNL20, described as a 20 GHz 2-port Vector Network Analyzer with a 5 kHz to 20 GHz VNA frequency range and 3.5 mm male test-port connectors [15][23].
【推論】For an automotive radar project, the VNA is best placed before radar echo-generation testing: use it to characterize the radar module’s board/interconnect/test-fixture signal paths—such as impedance, loss, crosstalk, material parameters, and cable/connector behavior—then use the radar echo generator for radar target/distance simulation and functional radar validation [4][6][10].
